- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–10 days.
- Model frequently underestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term horizon.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in correction; delay forecast drop by 1–2 days and reduce slope of decline.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 3+ days, model often overestimates; cap forecast at 1–2% below moving average for 5–10 days.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2) triggers model lag; forecast should adjust 1–2 days after sentiment change, not immediately.
